description: Let your AI agents use your real browser: an MCP server and a Chromium extension

files.content:
name: CI

on:
  push:
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  check:
    name: Typecheck, build and test
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      # Bun from package.json's packageManager field.
      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0
        with:
          bun-version-file: package.json

      # The MCP server and relay run under Node (cli/package.json engines), and the execute sandbox tests run in it too.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false

      - name: Install (extension)
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Install (cli)
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
        working-directory: cli

      - name: Typecheck (extension)
        run: bun run typecheck

      - name: Typecheck (cli)
        run: bun run typecheck
        working-directory: cli

      - name: Build (extension)
        run: bun run build

      - name: Build (cli)
        run: bun build.ts
        working-directory: cli

      - name: Test (extension)
        run: bun test ./test

      - name: Test (cli)
        run: bun run test
        working-directory: cli

      # The store zip and npm tarball the release workflow would build, with its artifact checks (permission allowlist,
      # no key, pairing code, source maps or test hooks), so a problem shows up on the PR rather than at release time.
      - name: Release artifacts check
        run: bun run release:check

  browser:
    name: Execute sandbox in headless Chromium (optional)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    # Informational: a real-browser check of the execute sandbox; a failure here doesn't fail CI.
    continue-on-error: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0
        with:
          bun-version-file: package.json

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false

      - name: Install (extension)
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Install (cli)
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
        working-directory: cli

      - name: Build (extension)
        run: bun run build

      - name: Build (cli)
        run: bun build.ts
        working-directory: cli

      # The Chromium the pinned patchright-core expects, with its system libraries.
      - name: Install Chromium
        run: node node_modules/patchright-core/cli.js install --with-deps --no-shell chromium
        working-directory: cli

      - name: Execute sandbox browser harness
        run: node --no-warnings test/execute-realm-browser.ts
        working-directory: cli

Let your AI agents use your real browser: your tabs, your logins, your extensions. An MCP server and a Chromium extension, for [opencode](https://opencode.ai) and any other MCP client. --- Agents get a `browse` MCP server. They open and drive tabs with Playwright, take screenshots, capture network traffic and record the screen, in background tabs grouped out of your way. When it's your turn (a login, a 2FA prompt, a payment), they hand the tab back to you and continue once you click **Continue**. It works in Chrome, Edge, Brave, Arc, Helium, Vivaldi, Opera and Chromium. ## Install ```sh npx @opencode/browse install ``` `install` puts the relay in your data folder (`~/.local/share/opencode-browser`), adds the `browse` MCP server to opencode, and connects the extension: 1. **Add the extension.** `install` opens Browse in the Chrome Web Store; add it to your browser. If it's already there, `install` opens its status page with the pairing code, so it pairs without copying anything. 2. **Restart opencode.** That's it. Ask an agent to *"open news.ycombinator.com and tell me the top story"*. Or paste this into opencode: *"Install browse with `npx @opencode/browse install`."* Requirements: Node.js 22.19+, a Chromium browser, and [opencode](https://opencode.ai) or another MCP client. **Updates are automatic.** The relay checks npm once a day and installs a new version in the background; it switches over when no agent is using the browser, without changing opencode's config or restarting it. Choose *Only tell me* or *Don't check* under **Updates** on the extension's status page (or `settings set autoUpdate=notify`, or `OPENCODE_BROWSER_AUTO_UPDATE=off`). `npx @opencode/browse update` updates now, and `npx @opencode/browse rollback` goes back to the previous version. The Chrome Web Store updates the extension. Betas: `npx @opencode/browse@beta install`. There's nothing to sign in to. The extension only obeys a relay that proves it knows this computer's pairing code (see [Security](#security)). If pairing didn't happen by itself, run `npx @opencode/browse pair` and paste the code on the extension's status page (right-click the toolbar button, then **Options**). ### From source For contributors, or before a release you need is on npm: ```sh git clone https://github.com/anomalyco/browse.git && cd browse && bun run setup ``` `setup` builds the extension and the CLI, adds the `browse` MCP server to opencode, and pairs the extension with the local relay. Two steps are left for you: 1. **Load the extension.** `setup` opens your browser's extensions page, shows the `browse/dist` folder and copies its path. Turn on **Developer mode**, click **Load unpacked** and choose that folder (on macOS, press Cmd+Shift+G in the picker and paste), or drag the folder onto the page. `setup` waits until the extension connects. 2. **Restart opencode.** This needs [Bun](https://bun.sh) as well. A checkout never updates itself: run `node cli/dist/cli.mjs update` in your `browse` folder (or ask your agent to update browse), then restart opencode. It pulls the new commits (fast-forward only, and never over local changes), rebuilds, and reloads the extension for you. The manual equivalent is `git pull && bun run setup`. When there's an update, `status`, `doctor`, the extension's status page and the agent (once per session) say so; browse checks the clone's remote at most every six hours. Set `OPENCODE_BROWSER_UPDATE_CHECK=0` to turn the check off. ### Other MCP clients `install` writes the server into opencode's config. For other clients, add an stdio server that runs the installed shim, which always runs the current version (from a checkout, use `/path/to/browse/cli/dist/cli.mjs` instead): ```json { "browse": { "command": "node", "args": ["/Users/you/.local/share/opencode-browser/bin/opencode-browser.mjs", "mcp"] } } ``` ## Using it - **Agents open their own tabs** in the background of the window you last used, grouped at the start of your tab strip under the agent's session name and collapsed unless you're looking at one. Agents can't switch you to their tabs or bring a window to the front; popups an agent opens join its group, and if one takes over your window you get your tab back. Tabs nobody touches for 10 minutes close by themselves (never while a script runs on them). - **Settings** (the extension's options page; each applies right away, to new tabs for window and grouping): - **Where agents open their tabs:** in your window (default), or *in a separate window* of their own that opens unfocused beside yours (on another display when there's no room on yours); their popups move there too. - **Grouping:** one collapsed group per agent session (default), *one shared group* for every agent ("Agents · 3", one per window, popups included; a handoff opens it), or *don't group* (agent tabs sit in the background of your tab strip; pin one to keep it). Tabs already grouped stay where they are when you switch. - **Close tabs agents haven't touched for:** 10 minutes (default), 30, 60, or *never*. Tabs a script runs on, a handoff waits on or a recording records stay open regardless. With *never*, an agent's `tabs_cleanup` without a time still closes only tabs idle for 10 minutes. - **Agent cursor:** off (default) or *always show* it on agent tabs. Pages can detect it while it's shown. Recordings still leave it out unless they ask for it (`cursor: true`). - **Human-like input:** on (default), or *off*: faster, but easier for sites to flag as a bot. - **Handoff notifications:** only while the tab is recorded (default), or *on every handoff*, as well as the card. The relay's environment variables below override the window, cursor and input settings; the options page then shows the value in effect and which variable set it. Agents can read and change these settings with the `settings` tool when you ask them to (`node cli/dist/cli.mjs settings get`, `settings set grouping=shared` on the CLI); the options page follows at once. The security switches below are environment-only, never settings. - **Hand an agent one of your tabs** by clicking the toolbar button on it. The badge shows **ON**; click again to take it back. While an agent works the badge reads **RUN**, and **WAIT** when it needs you. The button always works: a click while a script runs takes the tab back and stops the script. Agents can't close a tab you lent them. - **Handoffs:** the page shows a small card with the site's origin. Do the human part, then click **Continue** on the card or the toolbar button. - **Recordings show only the page.** Nothing from Browse is drawn while a tab is recorded: no cursor, no labels, no handoff card (you get a system notification instead; click it to go to the tab). If notifications are turned off for the extension, the card is shown after all, and the recording includes it. For a demo video, ask for the ghost cursor with `cursor: true` on `recording_start` (`--cursor` on the CLI). - **Status:** the extension's options page shows whether the relay is connected and paired, and can copy diagnostics. ## Tools | Tool | What it does | | --- | --- | | `execute` | Run Playwright code against the session's page (`page`, `context`, `snapshot()`, `handoff()`, …) | | `session_new`, `session_list`, `session_use`, `session_current`, `session_reset`, `session_delete` | Named sessions, each with its own tabs; they survive restarts | | `session_adopt` | Take over a tab you handed over with the toolbar button | | `session_allowlist` | Limit a session's tabs to the sites you name (also `allowedOrigins` on `session_new`) | | `network_start`, `network_status`, `network_stop`, `network_cancel` | Capture traffic to a redacted HAR | | `recording_start`, `recording_stop`, `recording_status`, `recording_cancel` | Record a tab to MP4 or WebM (`cursor: true` draws the ghost cursor) | | `flight_recorder_start`, `flight_recorder_save_last`, … | Keep the last minute of video, save it when something breaks | | `secrets_list` | Site secrets you stored, and the Deadbolt logins you granted, for the session's sites; agents type them with `secrets.type()` only on their sites, without seeing them | | `signin` | Sign in to a site with a Deadbolt login you granted, in one step, without the agent seeing any value | | `secrets_status`, `secrets_refresh`, `secrets_run` | Reuse captured credentials while keeping their values out of transcripts and artifacts | | `tabs_cleanup` | Close the agent's idle tabs | | `settings` | Read or change the settings below when the user asks (never the security switches); the options page updates live | | `status`, `skill` | Connection status, and the full agent guide | The agent guide is [`cli/skills/browse/SKILL.md`](cli/skills/browse/SKILL.md). Everything is also a CLI: `node cli/dist/cli.mjs --help`. ## How it works The agent talks to the `browse` MCP server over stdio. The server hands each command to the relay on `127.0.0.1:19988`, and the extension, connected to the relay over a WebSocket, runs it in your browser through `chrome.debugger`. - **The relay** (`cli/`) is a local Chrome DevTools endpoint backed by the extension. It keeps named sessions, handoffs, recordings, network capture and a journal, and starts on demand. - **The extension** (`src/`) connects to the relay and runs its commands through `chrome.debugger`. It keeps agent tabs in collapsed groups (or their own window), closes idle ones, and shows the toolbar badge and the handoff card. - **Quiet in the page.** `execute` uses [Patchright](https://github.com/Kaliiiiiiiiii-Vinyzu/patchright), which hides the usual automation tells (`navigator.webdriver`, the `Runtime.enable` leak), and the relay drops Patchright's media emulation overrides. The extension adds nothing to pages you browse; in agent tabs it adds nothing to the DOM except the handoff card while a handoff waits (and the ghost cursor when asked for). Both live in a closed shadow root on an anonymous element, drawn from an isolated world. Input moves like a person: curved mouse paths, paced typing, gliding scroll (turn *Human-like input* off on the options page, or `OPENCODE_BROWSER_HUMAN_INPUT=0`, for full speed). This makes an agent hard to spot, not impossible: the browser shows its "started debugging" bar while the debugger is attached, focus emulation keeps background agent tabs "visible", the card and cursor elements exist while shown, and `fillInput`'s fallback dispatches synthetic events (it warns when it does). Permissions: `debugger`, `tabs`, `tabGroups`, `storage`, `alarms`, `offscreen` and `tabCapture` (recordings), `scripting` (to add the handoff script only to tabs agents use, never to every page), `webNavigation` (to keep popups agents open with their other tabs), `notifications` (to tell you an agent needs you while it records a tab), and access to all sites so agents can work wherever you ask. Nothing leaves your computer except what your agent sends to its model provider; see the [privacy policy](store/privacy-policy.md). ## Security Browse drives the browser you're signed in to, so it assumes that what an agent reads (a web page, an email) may try to steer it, and that other programs on your computer may try to use the relay. - **Relay token.** Every HTTP request and CDP connection to the relay needs the token in `~/.local/share/opencode-browser/relay-token` (readable only by you): an `Authorization: Bearer` header, or `?opencodeBrowserToken=` on the CDP WebSocket URL. The MCP server and CLI read it for you. The relay listens on `127.0.0.1` only and refuses cross-site browser requests and foreign `Host` headers. - **Pairing.** The extension and the relay prove to each other that they know the same pairing code (HMAC over fresh nonces) before the extension obeys anything, so a program that grabs the port first can't drive your browser. The relay accepts only the two published extension IDs (plus any listed in `OPENCODE_BROWSER_EXTENSION_ORIGINS`). - **Sandboxed `execute`.** Agent code runs in a separate JavaScript realm that isolates it from Node: it isn't given `process`, `require`, `import()`, `fs` or network modules, only a `files` helper and Playwright file options limited to the temp directory, not Browse's data. The sandbox is a defense in depth, not a hard security boundary: treat code an agent runs as code running as you. The relay starts with an allowlisted environment (the basics plus `OPENCODE_BROWSER_*`, proxy variables and CA certificate paths), so your API keys aren't in it. - **CDP guardrails.** Cookie reads return only cookies for the session's own pages; cookie writes are limited to those hosts. Clearing cookies, cache or site data, and closing the browser, are always refused. `page.bringToFront()` is refused so agents can't raise windows over your work. - **Domain allowlists (opt-in).** `session new --allow-origin example.com` (or `session allow`, or `allowedOrigins` on `session_new` / `session_allowlist`) limits where a session's tabs go. The relay refuses agent navigations and new tabs to other hosts, stops or blanks links, redirects and script navigations that leave the list, and closes popups that open elsewhere. Private, loopback and link-local addresses need an entry naming that exact host; names are resolved first and the document's real remote IP is checked, against DNS rebinding. Subresources (images, fetch, iframes, workers) are not blocked: request interception is shared with Playwright's `page.route()`, so the relay can't own it reliably. Browsing through a local proxy makes every document look like it came from the proxy's address, so name the hosts you need exactly. - **Site secrets.** `opencode-browser secrets add --origin https://example.com` stores a password, key or (with `--totp`) a TOTP seed, read from stdin or a hidden prompt, in `~/.local/share/opencode-browser/site-secrets/` (0700/0600). An agent types it with `secrets.type(locator, "")`: the relay checks the field's frame URL from the browser's frame tree against the secret's origins (and the session's allowlist) right before it inserts the value, so a cross-origin iframe or a redirect gets nothing. The value never enters the execute sandbox, results, logs, journals or HARs. Once typed it is in the page, where page script could read it, so pair secrets with an allowlist (execute warns when you don't). A stored TOTP seed makes 2FA one factor; keep handing 2FA to yourself when you can. `secrets list` and `secrets remove` manage them. - **Deadbolt sign-ins.** With [Deadbolt](https://github.com/anomalyco/deadbolt), agents can sign in unattended with the logins you allow. Connect once with `opencode-browser deadbolt connect` (it runs `deadbolt agents add-client browse`, which asks for Touch ID or your passphrase and refuses AI agents) and allow logins in Deadbolt: `deadbolt agents allow github.com` lets agents use that site's logins (username, password, one-time code and passkeys, unless you narrow it with `--login `, `--fields`, `--no-passkeys` or `--expires 30d`), and `deadbolt agents allow --all` lets them use every login. Only you can grant; `deadbolt agents grants` and `deadbolt agents revoke ` manage grants, and every fill is in `deadbolt activity`. Agents call the `signin` tool (or `secrets.signIn()` in execute): the relay does the whole sign-in inside one call (username, submit, password, an authenticator code including split code boxes, "Use password instead", and Sign in with Google when a Google login is granted) and returns only `{status, step, reason}`. It stops with `needs_user` for captchas, codes sent by SMS or email, push approvals and new-device checks, for you to finish after a handoff, and when it stops after a fill it empties the password and code fields first. `secrets.type(locator, "deadbolt:[/]", { field })` types one value for forms `signin` misreads: a username on its own, a password or code only with `{ submit: true }` (typed, submitted and cleared in the same call). In tabs agents opened, a site's passkey request (`navigator.credentials.get`) is answered by Deadbolt when a grant covers the site's passkeys (user presence only, never user verification, so sites that require verification fall back); otherwise it fails as if you dismissed it. With several passkeys for a site the agent names the account (`signin` with `username`, or `secrets.usePasskey({ site, username })`); without one, `signin` returns `needs_choice` with the accounts. Agents can't use the browser's WebAuthn debugging methods. **Trust model.** Values never pass through the agent's results, logs, journals or HARs, and the agent never gets them by accident or from a prompt-injected page: the relay checks each field's frame origin from the browser's frame tree (and the session allowlist) before it asks Deadbolt, which checks the grant and the login's URLs against that origin again, and nothing is left typed in a page after a step. But a value typed into a page is in a page the agent controls: a deliberately hostile agent with page-script or network hooks could capture it. Browse refuses Deadbolt passwords and codes in a session whose code set up request interception or listeners, init scripts, exposed functions or a raw CDP session, but it can't tell a listener added with `page.evaluate()` from a normal read, and execute code run with `OPENCODE_BROWSER_ALLOW_NODE=1` can read anything the relay can. So grant only what you'd let that agent use anyway, and remember a captured value outlives revoking the grant or locking Deadbolt: change the password if you suspect it. The client token is stored 0600 in `~/.local/share/opencode-browser/deadbolt-client.json`: any program running as you that can read it can use the logins you granted (never anything else), which is the price of unattended use. Pair grants with a session allowlist. Locking Deadbolt pauses all agent sign-ins. `opencode-browser deadbolt status` shows the connection; `deadbolt disconnect` removes it. The relay finds Deadbolt's socket by Deadbolt's own rules (`$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/deadbolt…/agent.sock`, else `$TMPDIR/deadbolt…-/agent.sock`, with `DEADBOLT_HOME` taken into account) or `OPENCODE_BROWSER_DEADBOLT_SOCKET`. - **Bot challenges.** After a navigation, execute reports Cloudflare, Akamai, DataDome, PerimeterX, Imperva, AWS WAF, captcha walls and "access denied" pages in `aftermath.challenge`. It waits up to 15 s (`OPENCODE_BROWSER_CHALLENGE_WAIT_MS`) for checks the browser clears by itself, and tells the agent to hand interactive ones to you. It never solves them. - **Your tabs stay yours.** Agents use only tabs they opened or you lent them. The toolbar button always takes a tab back; only a real click on the card or the toolbar button finishes a handoff, so a page can't fake it. - **Less on disk.** Session journals are private (0700/0600), redact typed passwords, codes and tokens, and are pruned after 14 days (200 at most). HARs replace credentials with references; typed passwords and one-time codes are never stored. Secret profiles keep values out of transcripts and artifacts, but anything that runs with them (like `secrets_run`) can use them. `secrets_run` commands get the relay's allowlisted environment plus the profile's `BC_SECRET_N` values, not the environment you started opencode with: `PATH`, `HOME`, locale, `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY`, `SSL_CERT_FILE`, `SSL_CERT_DIR` and `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` pass through; other variables (API keys included) don't. Escape hatches. Set them in the environment you start opencode (or your MCP client) from; the relay inherits `OPENCODE_BROWSER_*` variables. Run `node cli/dist/cli.mjs relay restart` after changing them: | Variable | Effect | | --- | --- | | `OPENCODE_BROWSER_ALLOW_NODE=1` | Run `execute` code with full Node access (`process`, `fs`, `import()`, any file path) | | `OPENCODE_BROWSER_ALLOW_ALL_COOKIES=1` | Let sessions read and write every cookie in the profile | | `OPENCODE_BROWSER_ALLOW_FOREGROUND=1` | Allow `page.bringToFront()` | | `OPENCODE_BROWSER_AGENT_WINDOW=separate` | Open agent tabs in a separate window (`current`: in the user's window), overriding the options page's *Where agents open their tabs* | | `OPENCODE_BROWSER_EXECUTE_SLICE_MS=2000` | Longest `execute` JavaScript may run without yielding before it is stopped (50 to 60000; every session waits meanwhile) | | `OPENCODE_BROWSER_GHOST_CURSOR=1` | Show the agent cursor on every agent tab outside recordings (pages can see it); `0` keeps it off. Overrides the options page's *Agent cursor* | | `OPENCODE_BROWSER_AUTO_UPDATE=notify` | npm installs: only show new versions (`off`: don't check; `on`: install them when idle, the default). Overrides the status page's *Updates* | | `OPENCODE_BROWSER_HUMAN_INPUT=0` | Send input at full speed instead of human-like paths and pacing; `1` keeps them on. Overrides the options page's *Human-like input* | | `OPENCODE_BROWSER_CHALLENGE_WAIT_MS=15000` | How long `execute` waits for a bot check the browser clears by itself (0 to 60000; 0 reports it without waiting) | ## Troubleshooting - `node cli/dist/cli.mjs status` shows the relay, the extension and every tab agents can use. - `node cli/dist/cli.mjs doctor` checks the install. - Logs: `~/.local/share/opencode-browser/logs/relay.log`. - Extension says another browser is connected: only one browser profile can be connected at a time. Close the other one, then click **Reconnect** on the status page. - Extension says it's not paired (or that the relay was refused): run `bun run setup` again, then reload the extension on your browser's extensions page. - **Load unpacked** fails, or the extension shows errors: load the `browse/dist` folder (built by `setup`), not `browse` itself or `browse/public`. `node cli/dist/cli.mjs extension` shows the right folder. ## Development ```sh bun install && bun run dev # rebuilds dist/ on change; reload the extension to pick it up bun run typecheck bun run test # the extension and cli/ test suites (bun test), no browser needed cd cli && bun src/main.ts status # the CLI from source bun run release:check # the store zip and npm tarball a release would publish, with its checks ``` `cli/` is the npm package `@opencode/browse` with its own lockfile. The extension and the package share one version; [RELEASING.md](RELEASING.md) has the release flow (`bun run release `, then push the tag). ## License [MIT](LICENSE)

# Browse privacy policy

_Last updated: October 28, 2026_

Browse is a browser extension that lets OpenCode, running on your own computer, use your browser. This policy explains what it handles and where that goes.

## What the extension handles
- **Page content, screenshots, network traffic, and actions** in tabs an agent opened, or tabs you let agents use with the toolbar button.
- **Recordings** of a tab, when you ask an agent for one.
- Which tabs agents opened, kept in your browser's extension storage so idle ones can be closed.
- The pairing code you enter on the status page (or that the installer put in the extension's folder), kept in extension storage. It never leaves your computer.
- A system notification, shown only when an agent needs you while it records a tab.
- **Site secrets** you choose to store with the `opencode-browser secrets add` command (a password, key or one-time-code seed, and the sites it may be typed on). They stay in a file on your computer that only your user account can read, and are typed only into fields on those sites. The extension never stores them; they are never sent anywhere except into the page you allowed, and your agent never receives them.

## Where it goes
- To **the OpenCode tools on your computer**, over a local connection (127.0.0.1). The extension only obeys a local relay that proves it knows your pairing code, and the relay only answers programs that hold its token, a file only your user account can read.
- OpenCode may send it to the AI model provider **you** configured in OpenCode, under that provider's terms. The extension itself doesn't choose or contact any provider.

Anomaly, the maker of OpenCode, doesn't run a server for this extension and doesn't receive, sell, or share your data. There's no analytics or tracking.

## Your choices
- Agents can't use your tabs unless you click the toolbar button on them. Click again to take a tab back.
- Remove the extension and run `npx @opencode/browse uninstall` (`node cli/dist/cli.mjs uninstall` from a checkout) to delete everything it set up.

## Contact
Questions: open an issue at https://github.com/anomalyco/browse.

# Stress testing browse

Scripts that stress browse end to end on a real, headed Chrome: a scenario suite, a soak with chaos, a fuzzer and a
smoke test. They run on a disposable Linux box (we use the exe.dev VM `browse-stress.exe.xyz`), never on a machine
whose browser or relay someone uses.

## The box

`exe/provision.sh` sets up an Ubuntu 24.04 box and is safe to re-run:

- Node 24 (in `/usr/local`), Bun (the `packageManager` version), Xvfb + fluxbox, Noto fonts (CJK, emoji), ffmpeg,
  x11vnc + noVNC, and Chrome for Testing stable (`~/chrome-for-testing/current`).
- `~/browse`: a clone of this repo, built and paired with `bun run setup`.
- systemd units (`exe/units/`): `browse-xvfb` (display `:99`), `browse-wm`, `browse-chrome` (headed Chrome with the
  extension, restarted on crash), `browse-vnc` (localhost only) and `browse-novnc` (port 8000).
- The relay is not a service: like on a laptop, any CLI or MCP call starts it on `127.0.0.1:19988`.

Chrome's flags are in `exe/chrome.sh`. The profile is `~/stress-profile` with developer mode on (browse's
`install`/`update` reload the extension, and Chrome disables reloaded unpacked extensions while developer mode is
off). Chrome also listens on `127.0.0.1:9222` (`--remote-debugging-port`): **that port is for the harness only**, to
click handoff cards like a person, stop the extension's service worker and count tabs, groups and debugger
attachments. browse never uses it.

Watch the browser at <https://browse-stress.exe.xyz/vnc.html> (exe.dev's proxy, private to people with access to the
VM; keep it private). Click **Connect**; no VNC password, the proxy is the gate.

```sh
wssh browse-stress.exe.xyz                                 # shell (wssh: ssh with the work key)
wssh browse-stress.exe.xyz 'node ~/browse/cli/dist/cli.mjs status'
wssh browse-stress.exe.xyz 'sudo systemctl restart browse-chrome'
stress/exe/deploy.sh                                       # copy this working tree to the box, rebuild, restart the relay
```

`deploy.sh` rsyncs uncommitted work too (nothing is pushed), keeping the box's `.git`, `node_modules`, builds and
pairing code.

## Runners

All of them run on the box from `~/browse`, write JSONL plus a `summary.md` under `~/stress-results/<time>-<kind>/`
and exit non-zero when something failed.

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `node stress/smoke.ts` | One MCP stdio session: initialize, tools/list, status, navigate, snapshot, fill, click, screenshot, network capture, recording, session_delete |
| `node stress/run-scenarios.ts [--only a,b] [--tag core] [--repeat N]` | The scenario suite (`scenarios.ts`) once, serially, a fresh session per scenario |
| `node stress/soak.ts [--workers 8] [--minutes 60] [--chaos-every 120] [--chaos a,b]` | N agents loop scenarios and real sites while chaos hits; metrics every 30 s |
| `node stress/fuzz.ts [--minutes 15] [--seed N]` | Malformed and hostile input at the HTTP API, CDP WebSocket, /extension and MCP tools |
| `bash stress/run-all.sh [soakMinutes] [fuzzMinutes]` | All of the above in order (run it in tmux) |

```sh
wssh browse-stress.exe.xyz "tmux new -d -s stress 'bash ~/browse/stress/run-all.sh 60 15 2>&1 | tee ~/stress-results/run-all.log'"
rsync -az -e wssh browse-stress.exe.xyz:stress-results/ /tmp/browse-stress-results/   # fetch results
```

Type-check the runners with `cli/node_modules/.bin/tsgo --noEmit -p stress/tsconfig.json` (they run with Node's type
stripping, no build step).

The scenarios serve a fixture site on `127.0.0.1:4510` (and `localhost:4510` as a second origin). Add a scenario by
appending to `scenarios` in `scenarios.ts`; tag it `soak` if it's safe to run beside other agents.

**Soak chaos events:** `relay-kill9` (kill -9; the next call restarts it), `sw-stop` (terminates the extension's
service worker), `close-agent-tabs`, `close-windows`, `chrome-restart`, `network-drop` (iptables drops ports 80, 443
and 53 for 10 to 25 s), `session-delete` (mid-task), `mcp-kill` (an agent's MCP server dies), `tabs-cleanup`,
`toolbar-stop` (the user clicks the toolbar button on an agent's tab, the kill switch). After each one a probe session
must run an execute within `--recovery-bound` seconds. Tasks overlapping a chaos window are left out of the success
rate. Pass criteria: calm success rate, every event recovered, no stuck workers, no relay restarts that chaos didn't
cause, bounded growth (relay RSS, fds, tabs per hour, fitted after a 5-minute warm-up), every tab a session holds
tracked for idle cleanup throughout, and no leaked tabs after the run (neither held by a session nor a window's active
tab).

`toolbar-stop` clicks through a test hook the extension has only when built with `OPENCODE_BROWSER_TEST_HOOKS=1`
(`exe/deploy.sh` builds it that way; release builds compile the hook out). It lives in the service worker's globals,
which the harness reaches over the debugging port; pages can't.

**Fuzz checks:** the relay never restarts or stops answering `/version`, nothing but `/` and `/version` answers without
the token, foreign `Host` headers and non-extension origins are refused, an unpaired `/extension` client never
displaces the real extension, and the MCP server never exits on bad input.

## Driving the box from a Mac

The MCP server can run on the box over SSH, so an agent on a Mac drives the box's browser:

```sh
node stress/smoke.ts --remote browse-stress.exe.xyz   # initialize, tools/list, status through wssh
```

An opencode MCP server entry for it (add it yourself; nothing here edits your config):

```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "browse-stress": {
        "type": "local",
        "command": ["wssh", "browse-stress.exe.xyz", "/usr/local/bin/node", "/home/exedev/browse/cli/dist/cli.mjs", "mcp"]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Use the full `/usr/local/bin/node` path: exe.dev's SSH `PATH` lists `/usr/local/bin` last.

## Stealth on a real Mac (manual, never CI)

The box above measures robustness, not stealth: Linux, Xvfb and Chrome for Testing look nothing like a user's
browser. `stress/stealth/run.ts` measures what sites can tell about browse on a real browser (Chrome or Helium on a
Mac). It opens public detector sites, so it never runs in CI, isn't part of `run-all.sh`, and should run only when
someone starts it.

```sh
cd cli && bun build.ts && cd ..                      # the runner uses this checkout's cli/dist/cli.mjs
node stress/stealth/run.ts                           # local probe, then every detector site
node stress/stealth/run.ts --probe-only              # only the local probe (no public sites)
node stress/stealth/run.ts --sites sannysoft,creepjs --wait-ms 10000
node stress/stealth/run.ts --sites-file my-sites.json --out /tmp/stealth-run
```

It drives browse the way an agent does, through the MCP server (`session_new`, then `execute` with `page.mouse`,
`page.click` and `page.keyboard`, so human-like input applies), against whichever relay `OPENCODE_BROWSER_HOME` and
`OPENCODE_BROWSER_PORT` select. Prefer a separate browser profile paired to its own relay (a different
`OPENCODE_BROWSER_HOME` and `OPENCODE_BROWSER_PORT`) over your everyday one, and note the browser version, macOS
version and network. Report a clean-profile run and a warm-profile run separately: clearance cookies change verdicts.

- **Local probe** (`stress/stealth/probe.html` and `snapshot.js`, served on `127.0.0.1`): records, while browse moves,
  hovers, clicks, types and scrolls: `screenX`/`screenY` against `clientX`/`clientY` (Chromium bug 40280325),
  `getCoalescedEvents()`/`getPredictedEvents()` emptiness, `isTrusted`, `movementX/Y`, click `detail`, inter-event
  timing and key dwell distributions; `nextHopProtocol` of the document against its subresources (document
  interception); navigator, User-Agent Client Hints, platform, `hardwareConcurrency`, `deviceMemory`, languages and
  timezone in the window against dedicated, shared and service workers; outer against inner window size, focus and
  visibility over the run; `Function.prototype.toString` of common APIs; automation globals, extra globals, `<html>`
  attributes and DOM nodes the page didn't add; main-world calls with foreign stacks; whether a console listener
  serialized an `Error` (the `Runtime.enable` tell); and the stack a main-world `page.evaluate` shows.
- **Detector sites** (`--sites` ids): `sannysoft` (bot.sannysoft.com), `browserscan` (browserscan.net/bot-detection),
  `creepjs`, `rebrowser` (bot-detector.rebrowser.net), `deviceandbrowserinfo` (are_you_a_bot), `pixelscan`,
  `fingerprint-demo` (demo.fingerprint.com bot firewall) and `recaptcha-v3` (antcpt.com score detector). Each gets a
  screenshot, a best-effort verdict read from the page (sites change; the screenshot is the ground truth) and any
  `aftermath.challenge` execute saw. `--sites-file` takes `[{ "id", "url", "waitMs"?, "extract"? }]`, where `extract`
  is the body of an async function run in the page that returns the verdict.

Results go to `~/stress-results/<time>-stealth/` (or `--out`): `summary.md`, `results.json`, `probe.json` and one PNG
per page. Keep them private: they describe the machine and browser.

# Releases browse: the Chrome Web Store zip and the @opencode/browse npm package, from one tag.
#   v1.2.3          stable: npm dist-tag latest, the store item (vars.CWS_ITEM_ID)
#   v1.2.3-beta.4   beta:   npm dist-tag beta, the unlisted beta store item (vars.CWS_BETA_ITEM_ID)
#   workflow_dispatch with dry_run (default true): verify, build, check and attest, never publish
# Tags come from `bun run release <version>` (scripts/release.ts). RELEASING.md has the one-time setup.
#
# verify -> build -> attest -> publish-npm (environment npm) ---------+
#                          \-> publish-cws (environment chrome-web-store) -> github-release
# The artifacts are built once in `build` and passed along; nothing is rebuilt after the checks.
name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+"
      - "v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+-beta.[0-9]+"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dry_run:
        description: "Build, check and attest only; publish nothing"
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: release-${{ github.ref }}
  # Never cancel a release halfway through publishing.
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
      channel: ${{ steps.version.outputs.channel }}
      publish: ${{ steps.version.outputs.publish }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # main's history, to check a stable tag is on main.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0
        with:
          bun-version-file: package.json

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false

      - name: Version, channel and whether to publish
        id: version
        env:
          EVENT: ${{ github.event_name }}
          REF_TYPE: ${{ github.ref_type }}
          REF_NAME: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          DRY_RUN: ${{ inputs.dry_run }}
        run: |
          version="$(node -p 'require("./cli/package.json").version')"
          case "$version" in
            *-beta.*) channel=beta ;;
            *) channel=latest ;;
          esac
          publish=false
          if [ "$REF_TYPE" = tag ] && { [ "$EVENT" = push ] || [ "$DRY_RUN" = false ]; }; then publish=true; fi
          if [ "$EVENT" = workflow_dispatch ] && [ "$DRY_RUN" = false ] && [ "$REF_TYPE" != tag ]; then
            echo "::error::A real (dry_run=false) release must run on a v* tag, not ${REF_NAME}."
            exit 1
          fi
          {
            echo "version=$version"
            echo "channel=$channel"
            echo "publish=$publish"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Releasing $version on $channel (publish: $publish)"

      - name: Stable tags are on main
        if: steps.version.outputs.channel == 'latest' && github.ref_type == 'tag'
        run: |
          git fetch --no-tags origin main
          git merge-base --is-ancestor "$GITHUB_SHA" origin/main || { echo "::error::$GITHUB_REF_NAME is not on main; stable releases come from main."; exit 1; }

      - name: Install (extension)
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Install (cli)
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
        working-directory: cli

      - name: Versions agree (tag, cli/package.json, package.json, manifest) and the changelog is ready
        env:
          REF_TYPE: ${{ github.ref_type }}
          REF_NAME: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          VERSION: ${{ steps.version.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          if [ "$REF_TYPE" = tag ]; then
            bun scripts/release-check.ts --versions-only --tag "$REF_NAME" --require-changelog
            bun scripts/changelog.ts check "$VERSION"
          else
            # A dry run from a branch: the changelog entry comes with `bun run release`, so only warn.
            bun scripts/release-check.ts --versions-only
            bun scripts/changelog.ts check "$VERSION" || echo "::warning::changelog/$VERSION.md is missing or not ready; a release tag would fail here."
          fi

      - name: Typecheck (extension)
        run: bun run typecheck

      - name: Typecheck (cli)
        run: bun run typecheck
        working-directory: cli

      - name: Build (extension)
        run: bun run build

      - name: Build (cli)
        run: bun build.ts
        working-directory: cli

      - name: Test
        run: bun run test

  build:
    name: Build and check artifacts
    needs: verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0
        with:
          bun-version-file: package.json

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false

      - name: Install (extension)
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Install (cli)
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile
        working-directory: cli

      # The store zip, the npm tarball (with the store item IDs baked in, cli/build.ts), the artifact checks and
      # SHA256SUMS: the same script as `bun run release:check`.
      - name: Build and check the store zip and npm tarball
        env:
          OPENCODE_BROWSER_STORE_ID: ${{ vars.CWS_ITEM_ID }}
          OPENCODE_BROWSER_BETA_STORE_ID: ${{ vars.CWS_BETA_ITEM_ID }}
          OPENCODE_BROWSER_STORE_LISTED: ${{ vars.CWS_ITEM_LISTED }}
          REF_TYPE: ${{ github.ref_type }}
          REF_NAME: ${{ github.ref_name }}
        run: |
          if [ "$REF_TYPE" = tag ]; then bun scripts/release-check.ts --tag "$REF_NAME" --require-changelog
          else bun scripts/release-check.ts; fi

      - name: Release notes
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ needs.verify.outputs.version }}
        run: bun scripts/changelog.ts notes "$VERSION" > release/NOTES.md || echo "No changelog entry for $VERSION (dry run)." > release/NOTES.md

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: release
          path: |
            release/*.zip
            release/*.tgz
            release/SHA256SUMS
            release/NOTES.md
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 30

  attest:
    name: Attest build provenance
    needs: [verify, build]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # Only this job mints an OIDC token for Sigstore, and it runs no repository code.
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      attestations: write
      contents: read
    outputs:
      url: ${{ steps.attest.outputs.attestation-url }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: release
          path: release

      - name: Checksums match
        working-directory: release
        run: sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS

      - id: attest
        uses: actions/attest-build-provenance@4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8 # v4.2.2
        with:
          subject-checksums: release/SHA256SUMS

      - name: Keep the attestation bundle with the release
        env:
          BUNDLE: ${{ steps.attest.outputs.bundle-path }}
        run: cp "$BUNDLE" release/attestation.sigstore.json

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: attestation
          path: release/attestation.sigstore.json
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 30

  publish-npm:
    name: Publish to npm
    needs: [verify, attest]
    if: needs.verify.outputs.publish == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    # Required reviewers approve before this job starts (RELEASING.md).
    environment:
      name: npm
      url: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@opencode/browse/v/${{ needs.verify.outputs.version }}
    permissions:
      # npm trusted publishing (OIDC) and the provenance statement.
      id-token: write
      # gh attestation verify, below.
      attestations: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: release
          path: release

      # The files about to be published are the ones this run built and attested (not just consistent with SHA256SUMS,
      # which travels in the same artifact): GitHub's attestation for each digest, signed by this workflow.
      - name: Verify build provenance
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.verify.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          for file in "release/opencode-browser-$VERSION.zip" "release/opencode-browse-$VERSION.tgz"; do
            gh attestation verify "$file" --repo "$GH_REPO" --signer-workflow "$GH_REPO/.github/workflows/release.yml"
          done

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          # npm 11.5.1+ for trusted publishing.
          node-version: 24
          package-manager-cache: false

      - name: Publish the built tarball
        working-directory: release
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ needs.verify.outputs.version }}
          CHANNEL: ${{ needs.verify.outputs.channel }}
          # Temporary until trusted publishing is configured on npmjs.com; then delete the secret and npm uses OIDC.
          NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
          # Only write a token when there is one, so an empty value never stands in for OIDC.
          if [ -n "$NPM_TOKEN" ]; then
            printf '//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=%s\n' "$NPM_TOKEN" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/.npmrc"
            export NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG="$RUNNER_TEMP/.npmrc"
          fi
          unset NPM_TOKEN
          if [ "$(npm view "@opencode/browse@$VERSION" version 2>/dev/null)" = "$VERSION" ]; then
            echo "@opencode/browse@$VERSION is already on npm; nothing to publish." | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            exit 0
          fi
          npm publish "./opencode-browse-$VERSION.tgz" --provenance --access public --tag "$CHANNEL"
          echo "Published @opencode/browse@$VERSION with dist-tag $CHANNEL." | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  publish-cws:
    name: Publish to the Chrome Web Store
    needs: [verify, attest]
    if: needs.verify.outputs.publish == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    environment:
      name: chrome-web-store
    permissions:
      contents: read
      attestations: read
    steps:
      # Only for scripts/cws.ts; the zip comes from the build job.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          sparse-checkout: |
            scripts
            package.json
          sparse-checkout-cone-mode: false

      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@0c5077e51419868618aeaa5fe8019c62421857d6 # v2.2.0
        with:
          bun-version-file: package.json

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: release
          path: release

      # The files about to be published are the ones this run built and attested (not just consistent with SHA256SUMS,
      # which travels in the same artifact): GitHub's attestation for each digest, signed by this workflow.
      - name: Verify build provenance
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.verify.outputs.version }}
        run: |
          for file in "release/opencode-browser-$VERSION.zip" "release/opencode-browse-$VERSION.tgz"; do
            gh attestation verify "$file" --repo "$GH_REPO" --signer-workflow "$GH_REPO/.github/workflows/release.yml"
          done

      - name: Upload and submit for review
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ needs.verify.outputs.version }}
          CHANNEL: ${{ needs.verify.outputs.channel }}
          CWS_CLIENT_ID: ${{ secrets.CWS_CLIENT_ID }}
          CWS_CLIENT_SECRET: ${{ secrets.CWS_CLIENT_SECRET }}
          CWS_REFRESH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CWS_REFRESH_TOKEN }}
          CWS_PUBLISHER_ID: ${{ vars.CWS_PUBLISHER_ID }}
          STABLE_ITEM: ${{ vars.CWS_ITEM_ID }}
          BETA_ITEM: ${{ vars.CWS_BETA_ITEM_ID }}
        run: |
          (cd release && sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS)
          if [ "$CHANNEL" = beta ]; then CWS_ITEM_ID="$BETA_ITEM"; else CWS_ITEM_ID="$STABLE_ITEM"; fi
          if [ -z "$CWS_ITEM_ID" ]; then
            echo "::error::No store item for $CHANNEL: set the repository variable $([ "$CHANNEL" = beta ] && echo CWS_BETA_ITEM_ID || echo CWS_ITEM_ID) (RELEASING.md)."
            exit 1
          fi
          export CWS_ITEM_ID
          bun scripts/cws.ts publish --zip "release/opencode-browser-$VERSION.zip" --version "$VERSION"

  github-release:
    name: GitHub release
    needs: [verify, attest, publish-npm, publish-cws]
    if: needs.verify.outputs.publish == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          path: release
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Create the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          TAG: ${{ github.ref_name }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.verify.outputs.version }}
          CHANNEL: ${{ needs.verify.outputs.channel }}
          ATTESTATION: ${{ needs.attest.outputs.url }}
        run: |
          cd release
          sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS
          {
            cat NOTES.md
            echo
            echo "## Install"
            echo
            spec="@opencode/browse"
            if [ "$CHANNEL" = beta ]; then spec="@opencode/browse@beta"; fi
            printf '%snpx %s install%s\n' '`' "$spec" '`'
            echo
            echo "## Verify"
            echo
            echo "Build provenance: $ATTESTATION"
            echo
            echo '```sh'
            echo "sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS"
            echo "gh attestation verify opencode-browser-$VERSION.zip --repo $GH_REPO"
            echo "gh attestation verify opencode-browse-$VERSION.tgz --repo $GH_REPO"
            echo '```'
          } > body.md
          prerelease=()
          if [ "$CHANNEL" = beta ]; then prerelease=(--prerelease); fi
          if gh release view "$TAG" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            gh release upload "$TAG" --clobber "opencode-browser-$VERSION.zip" "opencode-browse-$VERSION.tgz" SHA256SUMS attestation.sigstore.json
            gh release edit "$TAG" --notes-file body.md
          else
            gh release create "$TAG" --verify-tag --title "$TAG" --notes-file body.md "${prerelease[@]}" \
              "opencode-browser-$VERSION.zip" "opencode-browse-$VERSION.tgz" SHA256SUMS attestation.sigstore.json
          fi

/**
 * Per-client CDP target visibility.
 *
 * Each Browse session's sandbox connects as its own CDP client and
 * identifies itself with a Browse session id. Tabs created for a
 * session are owned by that session. Without scoping, every client is told
 * about every tab, so concurrently connected clients attach to and
 * double-initialize each other's pages, which makes
 * `newPage`/`setContent`/`evaluate` hang non-deterministically.
 *
 * Visibility rule:
 * - Session-owned targets are visible only to that session's clients.
 * - User toolbar-attached targets stay visible to every client, so
 *   `--target-url` recovery keeps working.
 * - Relay-created targets without a Browse session id belong to raw
 *   `connectOverCDP` clients. They are visible to raw clients and to a session
 *   client that does not already own a target, so explicit `--target-url`
 *   adoption can still find existing attached pages. Once a session has its own
 *   sandbox target, it must not attach to raw-client pages, or Playwright
 *   double-initializes the page on Chrome's single debugger attachment and
 *   `locator.evaluate` can wedge.
 *
 * Two simultaneous raw clients can still interfere with each other's tabs;
 * Browse sessions are the isolated, supported path.
 */
export function canClientSeeTarget(options: {
  readonly clientSessionId: string | undefined
  readonly targetOwnerSessionId: string | undefined
  readonly targetOwner: "relay" | "user"
  readonly clientHasOwnedTarget: boolean
}): boolean {
  if (options.targetOwnerSessionId === undefined) {
    return options.targetOwner === "user" || options.clientSessionId === undefined || !options.clientHasOwnedTarget
  }
  return options.clientSessionId === options.targetOwnerSessionId
}

export * as AuthenticatedOrigin from "./opencode-browser-client.ts"
export * as OpenCodeBrowserClient from "./opencode-browser-client.ts"
export * as SecretProfile from "./secret-profile.ts"
